bugs: Guest request to /api/posts without an Accept: application/json header returns 500 (Route [login] not defined) because the 'auth' middleware tries to redirect to a login route the app doesn't have. API guests should always get a 401 (routes/api.php:6, bootstrap/app.php has no redirectGuestsTo).
Empty query filters (?status=&tag=&per_page=) return 422 because the rules lack 'nullable', so a blank filter can't be treated as 'no filter' (app/Http/Requests/IndexPostRequest.php:14-16).
Tag names that differ only by case ('PHP' and 'php') become separate tags, even within one request (app/Models/Post.php:54).
antipatterns: app/Http/Controllers/PostController.php:36 uses ->response()->setStatusCode(201) by hand; a JsonResource for a model that was just created already returns 201.
app/Models/Post.php:24-26 sets the $attributes default status to the string 'draft' instead of the enum, which duplicates the database default.
Only PUT routes are defined (no PATCH), yet the update request treats every field as optional, i.e. a partial update (routes/api.php:9).
tests/Feature/PostApiTest.php:206 tests a model scope directly inside an HTTP feature test.
strengths: Thin controller using when() with $request->enum() and $request->integer(), plus latest()->latest('id') as a deterministic tie-breaker.
Modern Laravel 12/13 attributes: #[Fillable], #[ObservedBy], #[Scope]. Enum cast, Rule::enum validation, and enum default used in the migration.
Authorization is declared on the routes with ->can(), and the policy uses $post->user()->is($user).
syncTagNames uses a tidy collection pipeline: trim, filter, uniqueStrict, firstOrCreate.
Covers the main failure paths: 401, 403 (even with an invalid body), 404, 422, plus pagination and combined filters.
Index request validation caps per_page at 100.

bugs: distinct:ignore_case runs before trimming, so ['php', ' php'] is rejected with 'duplicate value' errors on every entry. That's harmless but slightly surprising, and the later unique() in syncTags is now mostly redundant (app/Http/Requests/StorePostRequest.php:21).
antipatterns: Deleted the base app's passing tests/Feature/ExampleTest.php, which was unrelated to the task.
Turned on Model::shouldBeStrict app-wide in AppServiceProvider.php:23, a global behaviour change outside the task's scope.

app/Http/Controllers/PostController.php:20 calls PostStatus::from($request->validated('status')) where $request->enum() would be more idiomatic, and line 24 uses validated('per_page') ?? 15 (a string) instead of $request->integer().
The default status lives in two places: the observer's creating hook (PostObserver.php:14) and the migration default (a hard-coded 'draft' string rather than the enum value).
Only PUT routes are defined (no PATCH) even though updates are partial (routes/api.php:9).
strengths: redirectGuestsTo returns null for api/*, so guests always get a JSON 401, and a test covers this.
The index rules are nullable, so blank filters are ignored, and a test covers this.
Returning new PostResource from store gives an automatic 201 with no manual status code.
Uses createOrFirst for tags, which is safe under concurrent requests given the unique index. The policy's delete() delegates to update().
Routes bind posts by slug ({post:slug}), and authorization is declared with ->can().

The most thorough tests: mass-assignment protection, unpublishing then republishing keeps the original published_at (using travel()), empty tags clears them, an array passed as tag is rejected, assertModelMissing and assertModelExists.

v.rationale: The two implementations are almost structurally identical: same enum, attribute-based model, observer, policy wired with ->can() on the routes, and FormRequests. Both test suites pass (impl-1 22 tests, impl-2 23). What separates them came from the probes. In impl-1, a guest request to /api/posts without a JSON Accept header returns a 500 because the auth middleware tries to redirect to a login route that doesn't exist; impl-2 sets redirectGuestsTo for api/* and returns a 401, with a test for it. Impl-1 also rejects empty filter values with a 422, while impl-2 accepts them as no filter, again with a test. Impl-2's tests go further: mass-assignment protection, unpublishing then republishing keeps published_at, and an empty tags array clears the tags. Impl-2 also uses the cleaner approaches of an automatic 201 and createOrFirst. Its weaknesses are scope creep (it deleted ExampleTest and enabled Model::shouldBeStrict app-wide) and slightly less idiomatic reading of the request (PostStatus::from and validated('per_page') instead of $request->enum() and $request->integer()). Impl-1 does read the request more idiomatically. On balance impl-2 has fewer real bugs and better tests, so it ranks first.
